after: ## Key idea: write about a play as a play
alt: Eight dramatic methods surround the audience at the centre: stage directions, entrances and exits, dramatic irony, narrators and framing, structure, dialogue, staging and setting, and characters as devices. Below, treating the play like a novel is contrasted with writing about what an audience sees on stage.
caption: AO2 rewards the playwright’s tools beyond words, each linked to the audience.

after: ## Applying the methods to the set plays
alt: Five rows, one per modern drama set play, each with a small icon of its distinctive method: a lighting change in An Inspector Calls, Alfieri addressing the audience in A View from the Bridge, past and present sharing the stage in Kindertransport, narration and physical staging in The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time, and music and drumming in Death and the King’s Horseman.
caption: Each set play has dramatic methods that only work on stage.

alt: An overview states that the Inspector’s power comes from moral authority and control of the drama. Four planned paragraphs follow the play from his entrance, through his control of structure and his direct language, to his exit and the final telephone call, each tagged with the dramatic method it analyses.
caption: Plan from entrance to exit, and tag each paragraph with a method.

alt: The sample paragraph on the Inspector’s entrance broken into five parts: a claim, the timing of the doorbell as a structural method, the lighting change to “brighter and harder” as a stage direction, the effect on the audience, and a link back to the Inspector’s power. Each part is tagged AO1 or AO2.
caption: Claim, methods, effect on the audience, link back: AO1 and AO2 in one paragraph.

alt: Three methods at the end of Act One of A View from the Bridge feed one effect: Marco silently lifting the chair, the shift in power between Eddie and Marco, and Alfieri’s framing that has already told the audience the story will end badly. Together they make the audience watch with dread. Below: claim, method, effect on the audience.
caption: Staging, a power shift and the narrator’s framing combine to create dread.

alt: A banner gives about 45 minutes per essay including planning. Four tiles: know where scenes and stage directions are, quote a few words rather than copying, plan three or four moments before opening the text, and limit each look-up to a quick check. The exam copy must be completely unmarked.
caption: The open book saves memorising, but only if you can find things fast.
